resources.string: Turn it on to clear cache of all apps, disable bloatware and speed up app launches.
Glide TV shows only real measured results. Android manages memory by itself, so freeing RAM is most useful right before launching a heavy app or game.
Some steps need Turbo on this Android version (cache of all apps / background apps of Android 14+).
To show app cache sizes, turn on Turbo or allow usage access for Glide TV.
Since Android 6, only system apps may clear the cache of other apps. Turbo gives Glide TV these rights through the TV\'s own debugging mode — no computer needed.
The operation failed. Details are in the Turbo log.
APKs are not selected by default — select them if you no longer need them.
This TV has no \"All files access\" screen. Turn on Turbo — Glide TV will grant it automatically.

Fire OS 5 does not allow disabling apps. Cleanup and RAM features still work.
A check mark means \"disabled\". Nothing is uninstalled — every app can be turned back on with one button.

Turbo uses the TV\'s own debugging mode (ADB) to get the rights needed for full cleanup. No computer and no extra apps are needed.

1. Press "Developer options" (or: Settings → My Fire TV → Developer options).
 If there is no such menu: Settings → My Fire TV → About → press OK on the device name 7 times.
2. Turn on "ADB debugging".
3. Come back and press "Connect".
4. A dialog "Allow USB debugging?" appears — check "Always allow" and press OK.

1. Settings → Device Preferences → About → press OK on "Build" 7 times.
2. Back → Developer options → turn on "USB debugging" (and "Network debugging" if present).
3. Come back and press "Connect".
4. A dialog "Allow USB debugging?" appears — check "Always allow" and press OK.

1. Settings → Device Preferences → About → press OK on "Build" 7 times.
2. Back → Developer options → turn on "USB debugging".
3. Press "Connect" and confirm "Allow USB debugging?" (check "Always allow").
4. If it does not connect: turn on "Wireless debugging" and use "Pair with code".

1. Settings → System → About → press OK on "Android TV OS build" 7 times.
2. Back → Developer options → turn on "Wireless debugging".
3. Press "Pair with code" here, then on the TV open Wireless debugging → "Pair device with pairing code".
4. Scan the QR code with your phone and type the 6 digits from the TV screen. The TV dialog must stay open.
Developer options are hidden. Unlock them first (see step 1).
Enter the code from your phone
The pairing dialog on the TV closes as soon as you switch apps, so the code is entered on a phone connected to the same Wi-Fi.
Or enter the code here (if your TV keeps the dialog open):

Open \"Pair device with pairing code\" on the TV first and keep it open.
Done! Turbo is on — go back to the TV.
Paired, but could not connect. Make sure Wireless debugging stays on and press \"Connect\".
No local network connection — connect the TV to Wi-Fi or Ethernet.
Connecting… If a dialog \"Allow debugging?\" appears, check \"Always allow\" and press OK.
Connected. Glide TV granted itself the required rights.
Debugging was not allowed. Press \"Connect\" again and confirm the dialog on the screen.
Could not reach the debugging service. Check that debugging is on (step 2).
Requesting root access… confirm it in the root manager.
Debugging on the TV will be turned off and Turbo will stop working until you turn it on again. Cleanup results stay.
Shorter animations make the TV menu feel faster. Requires Turbo.
Pre-compiles installed apps (Netflix, YouTube, IPTV…). Cold start becomes noticeably faster. After an app update, run it again. Requires Turbo, Android 7+. May take a few minutes.
